Test these items: sql-name regex for ViewDefinition.name, constant.name, and column.name, sql-expressions constraint: at most one of forEach, forEachOrNull, or repeat, required field validation for resource, select, column.path, column.name, constant.name, constant.value[x], and where.path, resource binding validation against FHIR ResourceType, fhirVersion binding validation against FHIRVersion, expectError official fixtures fail explicitly rather than being skipped, permissive versus strict validation modes are clearly separated. For DuckDB-backed FHIRPath/CQL surfaces, test both the native/C++ extension path and the Python fallback where both exist, and compare outputs between paths. For SQL-on-FHIR ViewDefinition chunks, test parser validation, SQL generation, DuckDB execution, and official spec fixtures/examples relevant to the chunk.

When the pipeline is fully complete, set workflow to null, set exit_reason, write all handoff files, and return control to the outer spec compliance orchestrator.

issues.spec_citation: SQL-on-FHIR v2 ViewDefinition.constant.valueDecimal (FHIR decimal precision); official validate.js valueDecimal type number
issues.evidence: parse_view_definition(json_str) with valueDecimal 3.14159 -> Constant.to_dict() emits decimal.Decimal; json.dumps(vd.to_dict()) raises TypeError: Object of type Decimal is not JSON serializable. dict-input parse keeps float -> dataclass inequality across entry points. Reproducer: .temp/qa/sof_vd10_historian_2026_08_23/ (round-trip probe). No production consumer; loud failure.
issues.root_cause: parse_float=Decimal (lossless-parse doctrine) propagates Decimal into to_dict output; stdlib json cannot losslessly encode arbitrary-precision FHIR decimals.
issues.resolution: Deferred with doctrine: Decimal is the canonical in-memory repr; callers serializing to JSON must use a Decimal-aware encoder. Recorded in AGENTS.md.

issues.spec_citation: FHIR integer JSON representation (no decimal point); official validate.js valueInteger {type: integer} (Ajv accepts 3.0)
issues.evidence: valueInteger: 3.0 rejected with typed ParseError 'valueInteger must be a JSON integer'. Ajv Number.isInteger(3.0)===true so official accepts. Stricter boundary, typed error, FHIR-consistent.
issues.resolution: Intended stricter-than-reference boundary per FHIR integer representation rules.
